messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@helixai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix shortpilot — we are close but burned through runway

Hi Rishi / Laura / Grace,

Quick update from our side: the Helix AI team has run into higher-than-expected token usage during the final week of our timeboxed pilot. The prototype tests triggered a data-parallel job that spiked usage; we currently sit at ~92% of the pilot allocation with four business days left. Procurement is pushing us to decide on an approach that won't block the production demo next Wednesday.

Options they asked about:
- Buy a short top-up (hours/credits) to finish the pilot
- Move to a one-time invoice to cover the overage and extend access for 7 days
- Convert remaining evaluation to a short-term reduced-rate extension (discounted)

I attached the usage CSV and a short runbook of what caused the spike (POC_usage_report.csv). Procurement emailed procurement@helixai.com and asked for an invoice path, but engineering prefers a credit/top-up to keep telemetry tied to the pilot.

Can you advise on (a) a pragmatic short-term pricing option and (b) whether we can offer a small one-off concession (discount or a handful of eng hours) if they pick the invoice route? They want to close this today.

Thanks — Ari
Senior Solutions Engineer
HelixAI

--
Attachment: POC_usage_report.csv (CSV, 28 KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Ari Patel <ari@helixai.com>, procurement@helixai.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix shortpilot — we are close but burned through runway

Ari — thanks for the heads up and for the usage file.

Short answer: we can support both paths but each has tradeoffs. Two workable options I recommend for immediate closure:

Option A — Credit/top-up (preferred):
- Quick top-up of 50k tokens (~$1,200) to cover the remaining run and final demo
- Applies immediately to the pilot; keeps metrics and attribution intact
- No contract amendment required; we invoice as a usage charge on next month

Option B — One-time invoice + 7-day access extension:
- We issue a pro-forma invoice for the overage and a 7-day short extension (temporary license)
- Because procurement requested invoice flow, we can offer a 10% one-time concession on the invoice amount
- This path requires legal billing flow but is acceptable for enterprise bookkeeping

Operational add-on: if Helix signs up for a short reserved block (Dedicated trial) within 30 days, we can credit back the 10% concession towards their first monthly invoice (one-time offset).

I've attached a short two-page PDF with the bridge options and numbers (proposed-bridge-options.pdf).

If procurement insists on invoice, confirm the billing contact and PO number and we will push the pro-forma invoice immediately. If engineering wants to remain on credits, tell me the token amount they want and I can provision the top-up now.

Available for a 15-min call if helpful.

—Rishi
Head of Sales (Pilot Programs)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed-bridge-options.pdf (PDF, 64 KB)

Rishi — thanks, that helps. Procurement is on the invoice route for audit reasons. They asked whether Redwood can do the one-time 10% concession you mentioned. If you can provide that as a line-item discount on the pro-forma, procurement will greenlight immediately and send PO. They also asked whether we could include one advisory hour (30–60 min) to review the demo pipeline — that would help us avoid another spike.

So their request is: pro-forma invoice + 10% concession + 1 advisory hour included. Can you confirm acceptance and estimated invoice total (after discount) so we can return PO within today?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Ari
